query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled dispersion of nano‐oxide particles via a tailored annealing process in a low oxygen partial pressure environment will enhance the creep resistance and corrosion stability of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy while maintaining its strength–ductility balance to meet aerospace fastener requirements.
generation.material_initial_state: The baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy exhibits a uniform, fine lamellar structure but shows limitations in long-term mechanical loading (creep) and corrosion resistance under extreme temperature fluctuations.
generation.intervention: Tailored heat treatment: Anneal the alloy at approximately 900°C in a controlled atmosphere with a low oxygen partial pressure (e.g., diluted air) for several hours followed by controlled cooling to induce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale oxide particles.
generation.conditions: Annealing at ~900°C under controlled low oxygen conditions (diluted air) for a predetermined duration with a subsequent controlled cooling rate to stabilize the nano-oxide dispersion.
generation.structural_mediator: A uniform dispersion of nanoscale oxide (e.g., Al2O3) particles precipitated along the lamellar interfaces, which act as pinning centers.
generation.mechanism: The nano-oxide particles hinder dislocation glide and grain boundary sliding by serving as pinning centers, additionally acting as local diffusion barriers to corrosive species. This dual effect stabilizes the microstructure against creep deformation and protects against surface corrosion, particularly under thermal cycling.
generation.predicted_outcome: An alloy exhibiting markedly improved room-temperature creep resistance and enhanced corrosion stability under extreme temperature fluctuations relative to the unmodified eutectic alloy, while retaining a satisfactory strength–ductility balance.
generation.baseline: The unaltered AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy produced by standard casting and thermomechanical processing, lacking any nano-oxide dispersion.
generation.boundary: Enhancements are expected only when the heat-treatment parameters (temperature, atmosphere oxygen level, cooling rate) are precisely controlled; deviations may lead to uneven precipitate distribution or detrimental phase changes, limiting the intervention’s effectiveness.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvements in creep and corrosion behavior remain to be determined, and scaling the process uniformly for industrial-grade component sizes requires further validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one processed with the tailored annealing protocol intended to disperse the nano-oxide particles and one baseline set processed normally. Subject both sets to accelerated creep and corrosion tests that simulate the extreme temperature fluctuations and prolonged mechanical loading expected in aerospace fastener applications.
measurements: Measure room-temperature creep rates over extended times.
Examine surface degradation and microstructural integrity via SEM/EDS.
Perform electrochemical corrosion tests (e.g., potentiodynamic polarization) to quantify corrosion rates.
Assess mechanical properties such as yield strength and ductility.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nano-oxide dispersed samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in creep rate and improved corrosion performance (with maintained strength–ductility balance) compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

proposals.intervention: Introduce a controlled dispersion of nano-oxide particles via tailored annealing in a low oxygen partial pressure environment
proposals.conditions: Heat treatment at ~900°C in an atmosphere with controlled oxygen (e.g., diluted air) for a few hours followed by controlled cooling
proposals.structural_mediator: Uniformly distributed nanoscale Al2O3 (or similar) particles precipitated along the lamellar interfaces
proposals.mechanism: The nano-oxide particles serve as pinning centers that hinder dislocation glide and grain boundary sliding, thereby enhancing creep resistance under long-term mechanical loading and impeding corrosive attack by creating local barriers to diffusion
proposals.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and room-temperature creep resistance, along with enhanced corrosion stability across extreme temperature cycles, compared with the baseline alloy that lacks such dispersion
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention directly targets the limitations by reinforcing the microstructure against creep deformation and corrosion while maintaining strength–ductility balance, fulfilling the demanding requirements for aircraft and spacecraft fasteners

proposals.intervention: Refine and align the lamellar structure by employing directional solidification during casting
proposals.conditions: Implement a controlled directional solidification process with a high thermal gradient (e.g., >10 K/mm) and moderate cooling rates to preferentially orient the lamellae
proposals.structural_mediator: A more uniformly oriented fine lamellar microstructure with refined interlamellar spacing
proposals.mechanism: Directional alignment of the lamellae promotes anisotropic load sharing and reduces the propensity for localized creep deformation, while the refined spacing enhances the yield stress and limits crack initiation for improved ductility
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced mechanical performance including better strength–ductility balance and improved resistance to room-temperature creep and thermal cycling, relative to the baseline cast alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By controlling the microstructural architecture via directional solidification, the intervention targets the mechanical and environmental stability issues (creep, fatigue under thermal fluctuations) that limit the alloy’s use in fasteners

proposals.intervention: Apply an ultrathin, conformal ceramic coating by atomic layer deposition (ALD)
proposals.conditions: Deposit a ~50 nm thick Al2O3 coating at low temperatures (<300°C) using ALD on manufactured components
proposals.structural_mediator: A dense, defect-free ceramic surface layer that adheres to the alloy substrate
proposals.mechanism: The ALD coating acts as a barrier to corrosive species and oxygen, thereby inhibiting surface degradation and oxidation under extreme temperature fluctuations; additionally, it mitigates surface-initiated creep or fatigue by homogenizing surface stress
proposals.predicted_outcome: Significant improvement in corrosion resistance and thermal stability while indirectly supporting the mechanical integrity by reducing surface degradation, compared to the uncoated baseline
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: The surface coating directly addresses corrosion and thermal cycling challenges and complements the alloy’s intrinsic properties without altering its bulk composition or structure

proposals.intervention: Minor alloying addition of refractory elements, e.g., 2–3 at.% molybdenum (Mo)
proposals.conditions: Melt-processing with precise addition of Mo under controlled atmosphere to ensure homogenized distribution, followed by standard thermomechanical processing
proposals.structural_mediator: A modified solid solution where Mo atoms segregate subtly at lamellar interfaces and within the matrix
proposals.mechanism: Mo atoms provide additional solid solution strengthening and can reduce diffusion rates at high temperatures, thereby enhancing creep resistance and oxidation/corrosion stability through improved stability of the lamellar structure under thermal cycling
proposals.predicted_outcome: An alloy with superior high-temperature creep resistance and improved corrosion behavior while maintaining the requisite strength–ductility balance, surpassing the performance of the original alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By refining the alloy’s composition with a refractory element, this intervention aims to stabilize the microstructure under extreme service conditions, directly targeting both mechanical and environmental reliability requirements

decision.rationale: Direction B directly targets the critical limitations by reinforcing the alloy’s microstructure against room‐temperature creep and corrosion while still preserving the inherent strength–ductility balance. By inducing a controlled dispersion of nano-oxide particles during annealing in a low oxygen atmosphere, the intervention both pins dislocations and creates barriers to species diffusion. Although process control is required, this approach is well-aligned with the demands for high performance in aerospace fasteners, without fundamentally altering the alloy’s bulk composition or processing route.
